subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should persisted per-session `/exec` fields be allowed to override later stricter global or agent exec security config after a Discord session resumes?
rationale: The source reproduction is clear, but current tests encode persistent session defaults and the fix changes security-sensitive precedence plus upgrade/reset semantics for existing sessions.

options.title: Clamp to operator policy
options.body: Treat global or agent exec security as the upper bound and clear, clamp, or ignore stored session fields that would exceed it, with focused migration or reset coverage.

options.title: Keep persistence as-is
options.body: Document that operators must reset affected sessions or run a repair flow to enforce changed exec policy for existing Discord lanes.

options.title: Add reset/doctor first
options.body: Ship an operator-facing session exec reset or doctor repair before changing runtime precedence for existing sessions.

recommendation.title: Clamp to operator policy
recommendation.body: Treat global or agent exec security as the upper bound and clear, clamp, or ignore stored session fields that would exceed it, with focused migration or reset coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history trail for the `/exec` session override behavior and tests points to steipete.
